evidence.quote:
I had found instead only a sense of horror and
oppression which threatened to master, paralyze, and annihilate me.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator describes his emotional horror and oppression upon arriving in New York.

evidence.quote:
Garish daylight showed
only squalor and alienage and the noxious elephantiasis of climbing,
spreading stone where the moon had hinted of loveliness and elder
magic
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts the beautiful nighttime appearance of the city with its squalid daytime reality.

evidence.quote:
this city of stone and
stridor is not a sentient perpetuation of Old New York as London is
of Old London and Paris of Old Paris, but that it is in fact quite
dead, its sprawling body imperfectly embalmed and infested with
queer animate things
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator concludes that the city is dead and infested with alien animate things.

evidence.quote:
there appeared to reside
some very remarkable qualities in the will of mankind; qualities
having a little-suspected dominance not only over the acts of one
apos
self and of others, but over every variety of force and substance in
Nature
evidence.paraphrase: The host explains an ancestor's theory that the human will has dominance over natural forces and substances.

evidence.quote:
he flouted the sanctity of
things as great as space and time and that he put to strange uses
the rites of sartain half-breed red Indians once encamped upon this
hill
evidence.paraphrase: The host describes the ancestor manipulating space and time using rites learned from local Indians.

evidence.quote:
he bargained with them and exchanged the free access of
his grounds for the exact inwardness of what they did; larning that
their grandfathers got part of their custom from red ancestors and
part from an old Dutchman in the time of the States-General
evidence.paraphrase: The squire investigates and negotiates to learn the origins and workings of the secret rites.

evidence.quote:
all the world is but the smoke of our intellects; past
the bidding of the vulgar, but by the wise to be puffed out and
drawn in like any cloud of prime Virginia tobacco. What we want, we
may make about us; and what we don
apost want, we may sweep away.
evidence.paraphrase: The host articulates a doctrine that reality can be shaped and dismissed by the trained intellect.

evidence.quote:
a flash of
heat-lightning played over the scene, and I looked out upon a sea of
luxuriant foliage
dash foliage unpolluted, and not the sea of roofs to be
expected by any normal mind
evidence.paraphrase: Through the window the narrator sees a past landscape of foliage instead of the present city.

evidence.quote:
Again the lightning flashed
dash but this time upon a scene not wholly
strange. It was Greenwich, the Greenwich that used to be
evidence.paraphrase: A second vision shows the historical Greenwich as it once was.

evidence.quote:
I saw the heavens verminous with strange
flying things, and beneath them a hellish black city of giant stone
terraces with impious pyramids flung savagely to the moon
evidence.paraphrase: A vision of the future shows a monstrous city with strange flying things and alien people.

evidence.quote:
forgetting every injunction to silence
I screamed and screamed and screamed as my nerves gave way and the
walls quivered about me
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator screams uncontrollably at the horrifying future vision.

evidence.quote:
It spread over the old man, too, whether from
the same source or because of his fear and vehemence, and I saw him
shrivel and blacken as he lurched near and strove to rend me with
vulturine talons.
evidence.paraphrase: The old man shrivels and blackens under the moonlight, transforming physically.

evidence.quote:
I saw the gleam of a tomahawk as it cleft the
rending wood. I did not move, for I could not; but watched dazedly
as the door fell in pieces to admit a colossal, shapeless influx of
inky substance starred with shining, malevolent eyes.
evidence.paraphrase: The door is broken open and a shapeless mass with glowing eyes floods in to seize the old man.

evidence.quote:
Then the floor gave way at last, and I slid gaspingly down into the
nighted chamber below, choking with cobwebs and half-swooning with
terror.
evidence.paraphrase: The house collapses as the narrator falls through the floor.
